skills.name: aii-kdense-ontology-term-resolution
skills.content:
# Ontology term resolution

## The rule

**Never write an ontology ID from memory, and never accept one without
checking it.** A plausible `UBERON:0002108` is a real term (small intestine)
that is not the liver; the ID is well-formed, the ontology is right, and the
metadata is silently wrong. Every ID this skill emits comes from a live OLS
lookup, and every ID it is handed is verified against OLS. Bioregistry,
Identifiers.org, ZOOMA and Ontobee answer prefix, landing-page and shorthand
questions; they never replace that OLS check.

All scripts use only the standard library, take single values or a file,
and write TSV or JSON. Run them from the skill directory.

## Which script

- "What is the term for `left ventricle`?" — `scripts/resolve_terms.py`
  (OLS).
- OLS missed lab shorthand (`PBMC`, `WT`) — `scripts/map_terms.py`, then
  `scripts/validate_terms.py` (ZOOMA proposes, OLS decides).
- "Is `EFO:0001067` real, current, correctly labelled?" —
  `scripts/validate_terms.py` (OLS).
- "Is `HPO` a real prefix? Does `HP:notanid` match the pattern?" —
  `scripts/lookup_prefix.py` (Bioregistry).
- "Which landing page should this CURIE open?" — `scripts/lookup_prefix.py`
  (Identifiers.org and Ontobee URLs from Bioregistry mappings).

## Resolve text to terms

```bash
python3 scripts/resolve_terms.py "liver" --ontology uberon
# query  rank  curie           label  ontology  match_type   strategy  defining_ontology
# liver  1     UBERON:0002107  liver  uberon    exact_label  exact     true

python3 scripts/resolve_terms.py --input tissues.txt --ontology uberon \
    --exact-only --format tsv -o resolved.tsv
python3 scripts/resolve_terms.py "left ventrical of heart" --ontology uberon --top 3
```

The search escalates `exact` (label and synonym), then `token`, then
`fulltext`, stops at the first strategy that returns anything, and reports
which one fired. `--exact-only` disables the ladder. `--branch
UBERON:0000465` keeps only descendants of that term.

**Read `match_type` before using a result** (decision rule of this skill):

1. `exact_label` or `exact_synonym` in the expected ontology, defining
   copy: accept; record the primary label, not the synonym.
2. `partial`: apply the normalisations in
   `references/curation-rules.md` and retry once. Accept a `partial` only
   when the retried string is an `exact_label`/`exact_synonym`; otherwise
   write the row as unresolved with the top three candidates and their
   labels in a notes column, and say so in the output.
3. Exact match in the wrong ontology (`hepatocyte` in a tissue column): the
   column mixes concepts; leave the row unresolved and report the category
   error rather than forcing a match.
4. Nothing: unresolved, with the reason. An unresolved row is a correct
   output; an invented ID is not.

## Validate existing IDs

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_terms.py UBERON:0002107 EFO:0001067 UBERON:9999999
# UBERON:0002107  ok         liver
# EFO:0001067     obsolete   obsolete_parasitic infection  MONDO:0005135
# UBERON:9999999  not_found

python3 scripts/validate_terms.py --input metadata.tsv --strict
python3 scripts/validate_terms.py --input tissue_ids.tsv \
    --branch UBERON:0000465 --expect-ontology uberon
```

Exit code 1 if any row failed, 0 otherwise, 2 on usage or network trouble,
so it works as a gate on a metadata file. With an id and a label column it
catches IDs that exist but are labelled as something else.

Statuses (verdict in brackets; `--strict` turns every warn into a fail):

- `ok` [pass]: exists, current, consistent with everything asserted.
- `matched_synonym` [warn]: the claimed label is a synonym.
- `imported_only` [warn]: the home ontology no longer asserts this ID.
- `not_a_class` [warn]: the ID is a property or individual.
- `not_found` [fail]: no such term.
- `obsolete` [fail]: `replacement` names the successor when one exists.
  Apply it only after checking its label: a replacement can be broader or
  narrower than the original.
- `label_mismatch` [fail]: ID and claimed label describe different things.
- `wrong_ontology` / `wrong_branch` [fail]: right kind of ID, wrong
  ontology or not under the required root.
- `malformed_curie` [fail]: not `PREFIX:local`.

## Check a prefix or compact identifier

```bash
python3 scripts/lookup_prefix.py HP HPO HP:0001250 HPO:0001250
# HPO:0001250  synonym_prefix  HP  HP:0001250  ^\d{7}$  'HPO' is a synonym ...
```

Bioregistry accepts synonym prefixes; Identifiers.org does not
(`HPO:0001250` is HTTP 400). Rewrite to the preferred prefix before handing
a CURIE to OLS. Landing-page columns come from Bioregistry mappings
(`providers.miriam`, `mappings.ontobee`), never from templating the
preferred prefix: `ORPHA:558` is a 400 at Identifiers.org, `orphanet:558`
a 200 (both checked 2026-09-24). This script does **not** say the term
exists; that is still `scripts/validate_terms.py`.

## Map lab shorthand (ZOOMA)

```bash
python3 scripts/map_terms.py PBMC --ontology cl --exact-only
```

`--ontology` is required: unfiltered ZOOMA annotate returned FOODON, XAO,
BTO and UBERON hits for `liver`, all at HIGH confidence. HIGH/GOOD hits are
candidates only; run `scripts/validate_terms.py` on every CURIE before
writing it down.

## API behaviour that misleads (verified)

Checked against the live services (upstream July-September 2026; the
counts re-checked on 2026-09-24). Detail and more traps:
`references/ols4-api.md`, `references/companion-apis.md`.

- OLS `exact=true` is exact **token** matching: `liver` in UBERON gives 161
  hits; adding `queryFields=label` gives 1.
- OLS `/search` never returns `is_obsolete` or `term_replaced_by`, even when
  named in `fieldList`; only the term-detail endpoint says whether an ID is
  current.
- `ontology=efo` returns MONDO and CL hits (ontologies import each other):
  filter on the CURIE prefix yourself.
- The same term appears once per importing ontology: deduplicate on
  `obo_id` and keep `is_defining_ontology: true`.
- The `obo_id` index has had holes: upstream saw `MONDO:0000001` return
  nothing by `obo_id` (July 2026); on 2026-09-24 it resolved. The client
  keeps the IRI fallback so a hole never becomes a false `not_found`.
- IRIs are not all OBO PURLs (EFO, Orphanet have their own namespaces):
  resolve IRIs, do not template them.
- A branch check does not keep cell types out of anatomy: CARO puts `cell`
  under `anatomical structure`. Constrain the prefix too.
- Identifiers.org rejects synonym prefixes (`HPO:`) and an encoded colon
  (`HP%3A0001250`): HTTP 400 for both on 2026-09-24.
- Bioregistry `preferred_prefix` is not the Identifiers.org namespace; use
  `providers.miriam` from `/api/reference/{CURIE}`, and leave the URL empty
  when that mapping is missing (OBA, XAO, ECTO).
- OxO: upstream found it returning an HTML retirement page with HTTP 200
  (July 2026); on 2026-09-24 `/spot/oxo/api/search` answered JSON again.
  Check the `Content-Type` before parsing, and treat its mappings as leads
  (see `references/curation-rules.md`).
- Ontobee search is an HTML page with no JSON API; do not scrape it.

## Choosing the ontology

MONDO for disease, HP for phenotype, UBERON for tissue, CL for cell type,
EFO for assay, ChEBI for compounds, NCBITaxon for organism, PATO for sex
and for `normal`. OLS ids that differ from the prefix (`HP` is `hp`,
`Orphanet` is `ordo`), branch roots for `--branch`, and the overlapping
cases are in `references/ontology-registry.md`. Submission schemas
(CELLxGENE, HCA, ENA checklists) pin field names and permitted ontologies
per version: read the targeted schema version rather than memory.

## Reporting

Give the ID **and** the label, the `match_type` or validation status, the
retrieval date, and the ontology version OLS served: `config.version` of
`https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/{id}`, or `config.versionIri`
when that is empty (UBERON on 2026-09-24). List unresolved
terms explicitly instead of filling them with the nearest hit.

## References

- `references/ols4-api.md`: endpoints, parameters, response fields, every
  verified OLS trap.
- `references/companion-apis.md`: Bioregistry, Identifiers.org, ZOOMA and
  Ontobee, and the traps that make a call look successful.
- `references/ontology-registry.md`: prefix to OLS id, branch roots, which
  ontology owns which concept.
- `references/curation-rules.md`: normalisations to retry, auditing a
  table, obsolete terms, cross-ontology mapping.

## Sources

- OLS4 API: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/help; OLS4 paper, Bioinformatics
  2025, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf279.
- Bioregistry: Hoyt et al. 2022, doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01807-3;
  https://bioregistry.io/apidocs.
- Identifiers.org: Wimalaratne et al. 2018, doi:10.1038/sdata.2018.29;
  https://docs.identifiers.org/.
- ZOOMA: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/spot/zooma/docs.
- CARO `cell` under `anatomical structure`: Haendel et al. 2008,
  doi:10.1007/978-1-84628-885-2_16.

Use when writing or checking any ontology ID (UBERON, CL, MONDO, HP, EFO, ChEBI, NCBITaxon, GO, PATO) in metadata, submissions or a paper. NOT for gene or protein identifiers (use aii-kdense-gget).

skills.content:
# Pathogen Variant Surveillance

## The rule

**Never state what is circulating, and never write a lineage name, from memory.**

Three things go wrong at once, and only the first is an ordinary knowledge-cutoff problem:

1. **Names post-date training.** The Pango designation list carries thousands of names and
   grows continuously (`lineage_notes.txt`, https://github.com/cov-lineages/pango-designation).
2. **The nomenclature is a live data structure, not a convention.** `XFG` is a recombinant that
   only resolves through `alias_key.json`; `PQ.17` unaliases to `XDV.1.5.1.1.8.1.17`. Neither
   expansion is derivable by reasoning — the mapping is a file that changes.
3. **Prior knowledge gets retracted, not just outdated.** Hundreds of names in
   `lineage_notes.txt` are withdrawn or redesignated (294 when upstream counted, July 2026). `PC.2` is now `LF.7.9`; `XFG.20` was
   withdrawn outright. A remembered lineage fact is not merely stale, it can be actively wrong.

Every number this skill reports is a count returned by a live instance, stamped with the data
version it came from.

## Scope

Surveillance data analysis for research. This skill describes sequences that were collected and
submitted; it does not produce clinical interpretations, outbreak-response recommendations, or
public-health guidance, and sequence counts are not case counts.

## Instances

One API shape covers every pathogen. `--instance` names a verified deployment; `--base-url`
reaches any other LAPIS instance.

- `sars-cov-2` — lapis.cov-spectrum.org (open GenBank data); lineage
  column `pangoLineage`, indexed.
- `h5n1`, `h3n2`, `h1n1pdm`, `influenza-a` — lapis.genspectrum.org;
  lineage column `clade`, not indexed.
- `rsv-a`, `rsv-b`, `mpox`, `measles`, `dengue`, `west-nile`, `hmpv`,
  `ebola-zaire`, `ebola-sudan`, `cchf` — lapis.pathoplexus.org; lineage
  column and indexing vary.

**Field names differ per instance and are never assumed.** Every script reads
`/sample/databaseConfig` at run time and picks the collection-date, submission-date and lineage
columns from what the instance actually declares. `dateFrom=` is correct on SARS-CoV-2 and a hard
400 on H5N1, whose collection date is `sampleCollectionDateRangeLower`.

## Scripts

Run from the skill directory.

- `scripts/resolve_lineage.py`: does this name still exist, what does it
  expand to, what is it descended from?
- `scripts/lineage_prevalence.py`: what share of sequences is this
  lineage, week by week, and is it growing?
- `scripts/mutation_profile.py`: what mutations does it carry, and how does
  it differ from another lineage?
- `scripts/reporting_lag.py`: how far back does the data have to go before
  it can be trusted?

All four take `--format table|tsv|json` and print provenance (instance, data version, resolved
field names, filters) to stderr, so `> out.tsv` keeps the data clean and the provenance visible.

### Start from the data, not from a remembered list

```bash
# no names: discover what is actually circulating in the window
python3 scripts/lineage_prevalence.py --top 5 --where country=USA --weeks 12
```

> note: discovered the 5 most common pangoLineage values in the window:
> XFG.1.1, XFG.23.1.3, PY.1.1.1, XFJ.3.1.2, PQ.17

This is the right first command for "what is circulating". Naming lineages up front presumes you
already know which ones matter, which is the assumption this skill exists to remove.

### Check a name before using it

```bash
python3 scripts/resolve_lineage.py XFG.23.1.3 PQ.17 PC.2 NOTALINEAGE
```

```
query        status     unaliased                        parent    recombinant_of  descendants  sequences  detail
XFG.23.1.3   current    XFG.23.1.3                       XFG.23.1  LF.7+LP.8.1.2   6            317        S:A1174V, on C29137T branch
PQ.17        current    XDV.1.5.1.1.8.1.17               NB.1.8.1                  23           931        Alias of XDV.1.5.1.1.8.1.17
PC.2         withdrawn  B.1.1.529.2.86.1.1.16.1.7.2.1.2  LF.7.2.1                  4            25         now LF.7.9; Redesignated as LF.7.9
NOTALINEAGE  unknown    NOTALINEAGE                                                0            n/a        no such name in the live nomenclature
```

(`detail` abridged; each real row also cites the lineage proposal it came from.)

Exit code is 1 if any name is withdrawn or unknown, so it gates a manuscript's lineage list.
Note `PC.2`: withdrawn upstream, yet 25 sequences still carry the label because the instance's
assignments lag designation. Both facts are true and both matter.

### Prevalence and growth

```bash
python3 scripts/lineage_prevalence.py "XFG.1.1*" "XFJ*" --where country=USA --weeks 16 --growth
```

```
lineage   week        n   total  proportion  ci_low  ci_high  coverage
XFG.1.1*  2026-05-04  42  80     0.5250      0.4170  0.6308   ok
XFG.1.1*  2026-06-15  3   49     0.0612      0.0210  0.1652   ok
XFG.1.1*  2026-06-29  1   30     0.0333      0.0059  0.1667   low
XFG.1.1*  2026-07-13  0   0                                   low
```

Proportions carry Wilson intervals because surveillance weeks are small. Weeks whose denominator
has not filled in yet are flagged `low` and excluded from the growth fit unless
`--include-incomplete`.

The window is widened to whole ISO weeks, and says so when it does. A window starting mid-week
would give a first row covering three days and a last row covering four, neither comparable to the
full weeks between them.

`--growth` reports a weighted least-squares slope of log-odds against time. It is **descriptive**:
it absorbs every change in who is sequencing, where, and how fast they report. It is not a fitness
or transmissibility estimate. No slope is printed for a lineage with too few observations — see the
trap table for why that guard exists.

### Mutations, and whether an assay still matches

```bash
python3 scripts/mutation_profile.py "XFJ*" --versus "XFG*" --gene S --since 2026-01-01
```

```
mutation  gene  position  verdict  prop_a  prop_b  n_a  n_b
S:L441R   S     441       gained   1.000   0.000   66   0
S:A475V   S     475       gained   1.000   0.000   68   0
S:K444R   S     444       lost     0.000   0.996   0    5031
S:Q493E   S     493       lost     0.000   0.998   0    5359
```

Works the same on a segmented genome — `--instance h5n1 --gene HA` or `--gene seg4`. Use
`--nucleotide` for primer and probe questions, where the codon is not the unit that matters.

### Decide how far back to trust

```bash
python3 scripts/reporting_lag.py --where country=USA
```

```
lag_days  mean_complete  min_complete  max_complete  cohorts
14        0.456          0.332         0.557         6
30        0.677          0.580         0.822         6
60        0.868          0.802         0.949         6
90        0.939          0.916         1.000         6
```

> 90% of a cohort has arrived by 90 days. Trust collection dates up to 2026-04-28; treat anything
> later as provisional.

Run this **before** quoting any recent prevalence. The curve differs sharply by pathogen and
country: on H5N1 the same measurement returns 0% complete at 14 days and 15% at 30 days, so a
"current" H5N1 picture is effectively blind for two months.

## Traps that produce silently wrong answers

Verified against the live API by upstream on 2026-07-27; the counts marked
2026-09-24 were re-checked then. Full detail: `references/lapis-api.md`.

- A bare lineage name excludes its descendants: `pangoLineage=XFG` gave 849
  sequences and `XFG*` 34,215 (2026-09-24).
- A trailing `*` needs a lineage index: on H5N1 `clade=2.3.4.4b` gave 64,404
  and `clade=2.3.4.4b*` gave **0** (2026-09-24), the same syntax with the
  opposite meaning.
- Field names are per instance: `dateFrom` is HTTP 400 on H5N1
  (2026-09-24), whose collection date is `sampleCollectionDateRangeLower`.
- Only `date`-typed fields take ranges: H5N1 types `sampleCollectionDate` as
  a string, so it has no `From`/`To` keys at all.
- Recent weeks are a sample of whoever reports fastest, not of what
  circulated: only 29% of a US cohort had arrived within 7 days.
- LAPIS roots recombinants: asking it for `XFG`'s parents returns nothing;
  only `alias_key.json` records `XFG = LF.7 + LP.8.1.2`.
- Withdrawn names persist in the data: `PC.2` was redesignated `LF.7.9`
  upstream while sequences still carry `PC.2`.
- An unknown name fails loudly only when indexed: indexed columns reject a
  typo with a 400; unindexed columns answer `0`.
- Mutation `proportion` is over `coverage`, not over all matching
  sequences: a poorly covered site can show 1.000 on very few reads.
- `/sample/aggregated` has no inherent order: `limit` without `orderBy` is
  HTTP 400 on genspectrum and pathoplexus but was accepted by cov-spectrum
  on 2026-09-24 (instances run different LAPIS versions). Never page an
  aggregate; sort client-side.

## Reporting results

State the instance, the data version, the filters, and the window — a prevalence figure without
them cannot be reproduced, because the underlying database changes daily. Give counts alongside
proportions, quote the interval, and say explicitly when a window is too recent to support an
estimate. "No reliable estimate for the last six weeks" is a legitimate and often correct answer.

## Sources

- LAPIS API and filter grammar: https://lapis.cov-spectrum.org/open/v2/swagger-ui/index.html
  and Chen et al. 2022, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btab856 (CoV-Spectrum).
- Pango nomenclature, `alias_key.json`, `lineage_notes.txt`: Rambaut et al. 2020,
  doi:10.1038/s41564-020-0770-5; https://github.com/cov-lineages/pango-designation.
- Wilson score interval: Wilson 1927, doi:10.1080/01621459.1927.10502953.
- Pathoplexus: https://pathoplexus.org/docs.
- The 90%-complete trust cutoff and the `low` coverage flag are this
  skill's decision rules, not literature.

## References

- `references/lapis-api.md` — endpoints, filter grammar, per-instance schema differences, the
  instance registry, and every verified trap in full.
- `references/lineage-nomenclature.md` — Pango aliases and recombinants, designation churn,
  Nextstrain clades, WHO labels, influenza clades, H5N1 clades and genotypes, and how the naming
  systems map onto each other.
- `references/surveillance-caveats.md` — reporting lag, sampling and ascertainment bias, choosing
  a denominator, interval and growth interpretation, and the conclusions this data cannot support.
skills.description: Answer what a pathogen population looks like now from live LAPIS instances (SARS-CoV-2, influenza incl. H5N1, RSV, mpox and more): resolve Pango names against the live alias and withdrawal lists, weekly prevalence with Wilson intervals, mutation profiles, reporting lag. Use when naming lineages, quoting prevalence or growth, or checking a mutation or assay target. NOT for phylogenetic inference (use aii-kdense-phylogenetics).
skills.compatibility: Python 3.12, standard library only; network: lapis.cov-spectrum.org, lapis.genspectrum.org, lapis.pathoplexus.org, raw.githubusercontent.com (public, no key); GPU: none

skills.name: aii-kdense-phylogenetics
skills.content:
# Phylogenetics: align, infer, root, compare

Decide by the rules below and log each choice with its reason; never wait
for confirmation. Every tool statement was checked on 2026-09-24 by running
MAFFT 7.525, IQ-TREE 3.1.4, FastTree 2.2.0 and ete4 4.4.0.

## Setup

Run from the skill directory.

```bash
uv venv .venv --python 3.12 && . .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -r requirements.txt     # ete4 compiles from source
```

ete4 has no wheels: if the build stops at `Python.h: No such file`, use a
uv-managed interpreter (`uv venv --python-preference only-managed`). MAFFT,
IQ-TREE and FastTree are binaries: install them with the pinned, checksummed
commands in `references/inference.md`, inside the workspace. Before
`import ete4`, set `XDG_DATA_HOME` to a workspace directory (taxonomy
databases and caches go there, not under `~`).

## Router

- sequences to a rooted tree with supports — run:
  `python3 scripts/phylogenetic_analysis.py seqs.fasta --out-dir phylo --type nt`
  (`--engine fasttree` for thousands of sequences); read:
  `references/inference.md`
- MAFFT strategies, IQ-TREE flags, dating, ancestral states, concordance —
  read: `references/inference.md`
- reroot, prune, stats, RF distance, draw an existing tree — run:
  `python3 scripts/tree_operations.py {stats,reroot,prune,compare,render,...}`;
  read: `references/ete4.md`
- ete3 code or habits, gene-tree duplications, reconciliation — read:
  `references/ete4.md`
- NCBI or GTDB names, lineages, taxonomy trees — read:
  `references/taxonomy.md`

## Decision rules

1. **Align with `mafft --auto`** unless the data force a strategy: E-INS-i
   for long unalignable insertions, G-INS-i for similar full-length
   sequences. `--auto` already scales with count and length (MAFFT 7.525
   wrapper). Keep IDs free of `():;,[]'"` (IQ-TREE renames them) and unique.
2. **Do not trim by default.** Automated column filtering often worsens
   single-gene trees (Tan et al. 2015, doi:10.1093/sysbio/syv033); trim only
   with a stated reason and method.
3. **Let ModelFinder choose** (`-m MFP`, IQ-TREE's default when `-m` is
   omitted; Kalyaanamoorthy et al. 2017, doi:10.1038/nmeth.4285) and report
   the chosen model from the `.iqtree` report. `-m TEST` is the smaller
   classic set without FreeRate models.
4. **Supports: `-B 1000 --alrt 1000`.** Call a clade supported only when
   SH-aLRT >= 80 AND UFBoot >= 95 (IQ-TREE manual; Hoang et al. 2018,
   doi:10.1093/molbev/msx281). UFBoot is not a standard bootstrap: never
   apply 70 % or 80 % to it. FastTree labels are SH-like local supports on
   0-1, not bootstraps. Report how many internal branches pass, out of how
   many (n - 3 for an unrooted binary tree of n taxa).
5. **Root on a biological outgroup** that is monophyletic in the inferred
   tree; midpoint rooting only when there is none, and say it assumes a
   roughly constant rate. The ML tree itself is unrooted.
6. **Compare trees unrooted** (`unrooted_trees=True`) unless both are rooted
   on a justified outgroup; report RF, max RF and the shared leaf count.
7. **One tree needs one history.** For recombining viruses or bacterial core
   genes, screen for recombination first (HyPhy recombination detection;
   Kosakovsky Pond et al. 2006, doi:10.1093/molbev/msl051) and analyse
   non-recombinant blocks.
8. **Dates need temporal signal.** With `--date`, if IQ-TREE logs that the
   rate reached its lower bound, report "no temporal signal" instead of
   node ages (LSD2: To et al. 2016, doi:10.1093/sysbio/syv068).

## Traps (verified 2026-09-24)

- `mafft --linsi`, `--einsi`, `--fftns`, `--fftnsi` — what happens:
  `Unknown option`, MAFFT exits 1 (upstream's script and SKILL.md used
  them); do instead: `--localpair --maxiterate 1000` etc., or call the
  `linsi` program
- rerooting a tree whose support was read as names (ete4 parser 1) or as
  IQ-TREE pairs (`multisupport`) — what happens: ete4 moves only `dist` and
  `support`, so the labels silently land on the wrong splits (the `(A,B)`
  pair ended up on `(A,B,C)`); do instead: `set_outgroup(node,
  bprops=["multisupport"])`, as `scripts/tree_operations.py reroot` does
  (it refuses parser-1 trees whose names look like support)
- `Tree(open("x.treefile"))` on an IQ-TREE `-B --alrt` tree — what happens:
  parser 0 raises `NewickError` on `97.5/94`, parser 1 reads the pair as a
  name; do instead: `parser="multisupport"`
- `t1.robinson_foulds(t2)` — what happens: rooted by default, so two
  rootings of one unrooted tree score RF 2; do instead:
  `unrooted_trees=True` (the script's default)
- `robinson_foulds(..., min_support_t1=x)` on a `multisupport` tree — what
  happens: `support` is `None`, counted as 0, every branch dropped; do
  instead: copy the UFBoot value into `node.support` first
- `iqtree3 -B 500` — what happens: aborts, `#replicates must be >= 1000`;
  do instead: 1000 or more
- `iqtree3 --clock-test` — what happens: `Invalid "--clock-test" option` in
  3.1.4; `--date-ci 95` means 95 resampling replicates, not a 95 % interval
- `iqtree3 -o Outg` — what happens: only the drawing of `.treefile`
  changes; the tree stays unrooted; do instead: root in ete4
- `len(tree) - len(leaves)` for internal nodes — what happens: always 0,
  `len(tree)` counts leaves; do instead: count non-leaf nodes in `traverse()`
- `PhyloTree(nwk)` then species methods — what happens: `leaf.species` is
  `None` (ETE 3 used the first three letters); do instead: pass
  `sp_naming_function=`
- `NCBITaxa()` on first use — what happens: downloads taxdump to
  `~/.local/share/ete` with no timeout and no MD5 check, and writes temp
  files into the current directory; do instead: see `references/taxonomy.md`

## Scripts

`scripts/phylogenetic_analysis.py` (MAFFT, then IQ-TREE or FastTree, then
ete4 rooting) refuses before running anything (exit 2) on: fewer than 4
sequences, duplicate IDs, IDs IQ-TREE would rename, an unknown MAFFT
strategy, UFBoot below 1000, an outgroup not in the input, missing binaries.
It writes `<stem>.aln.fasta`, the inference files, `<stem>.rooted.nwk`
(labels `SH-aLRT/UFBoot`, re-read with `--parser multisupport`) and
`<stem>.run.json` (commands, tool versions, model, rooting, support counts).

```bash
python3 scripts/phylogenetic_analysis.py seqs.fasta --out-dir phylo --type nt \
    --outgroup Outg1,Outg2 --threads 4 --seed 1
python3 scripts/phylogenetic_analysis.py aln.fasta --aligned --out-dir phylo --type aa
```

`scripts/tree_operations.py` subcommands: `stats` (counts, polytomies,
branch lengths, support per scale, duplicate or unnamed leaves), `ascii`,
`leaves`, `convert`, `reroot` (`--midpoint` or `--outgroup`), `prune`
(`--keep`/`--keep-file`, refuses absent or duplicated names), `compare`
(unrooted RF by default, `--rooted` to opt in), `render` (PNG/SVG/PDF,
headless Qt). Unknown or ambiguous names exit 2.

```bash
python3 scripts/tree_operations.py reroot phylo/x.treefile rooted.nwk \
    --parser multisupport --outgroup Outg1
python3 scripts/tree_operations.py compare a.nwk b.nwk --parser-a multisupport
python3 scripts/tree_operations.py render rooted.nwk tree.svg \
    --parser multisupport --support-prop multisupport
```

## Reporting

State the aligner and strategy, trimming (or none), model and criterion
(BIC), inference program and version, support method and thresholds, the
number of supported branches, the rooting method, and the RF convention.
Figures of annotated trees go through aii-data-fig-gen; `render` gives the
tree panel.

## References

- `references/inference.md`: binary installs with checksums, MAFFT
  strategies, IQ-TREE flags and outputs, support scales, dating, ASR,
  concordance factors, FastTree, common failures.
- `references/ete4.md`: ETE 3 to ete4 renames, Newick parsers, rooting with
  branch properties, RF, gene-tree events and reconciliation, drawing.
- `references/taxonomy.md`: NCBI/GTDB databases in the workspace and the
  silent failures of name translation.
skills.description: Infer and work with phylogenetic trees: MAFFT alignment, IQ-TREE 3 ModelFinder with UFBoot/SH-aLRT support (or FastTree), then ete4 for rooting, pruning, RF comparison, gene-tree events and NCBI/GTDB taxonomy, keeping support values on the right branches. Use when building a tree from sequences, rooting or comparing trees, reading branch support, or dating tips. NOT for diversity or UniFrac on microbiome tables (use aii-kdense-scikit-bio).
skills.compatibility: Python 3.12, uv; ete4==4.4.0 (sdist: needs a C compiler and Python headers) and PyQt6 for drawing, pinned in requirements.txt; MAFFT 7.526, IQ-TREE 3.1.4, FastTree 2.2.0 binaries from pinned release URLs; network: downloads only; GPU: none.

skills.name: aii-kdense-polars-bio
skills.content:
# polars-bio: interval operations on Polars

polars-bio (https://biodatageeks.org/polars-bio/) runs interval operations
and bioinformatics readers on Apache DataFusion and returns Polars frames.
Every behaviour below was checked on polars-bio 0.36.0 with polars 1.44 on
2026-09-24; the unit tests pin the traps.

## Setup

```bash
uv venv .venv --python 3.12 && . .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -r <skill-dir>/requirements.txt
```

## The coordinate rule

polars-bio carries the coordinate system as metadata on each frame, and its
default is **1-based inclusive**
(`pb.get_option("datafusion.bio.coordinate_system_zero_based")` is `false`).

- `read_*` / `scan_*` convert to the configured system on read and attach
  metadata: `pb.read_bed` turns BED `chr1 0 10` into `start=1, end=10`.
  Pass `use_zero_based=True` to keep BED numbers as they are.
- A hand-built `pl.DataFrame` has **no metadata**: interval operations fall
  back to the global setting (1-based) and only emit a `UserWarning`. BED
  numbers typed into such a frame are therefore off by one: bookended
  `[0,10)` and `[10,20)` come back as overlapping. Always set it:
  `df.config_meta.set(coordinate_system_zero_based=True)`.
- `pb.set_option("datafusion.bio.coordinate_system_check", True)` turns the
  missing-metadata warning into `MissingCoordinateSystemError`. Set it at
  the start of every script. Inputs in different systems raise
  `CoordinateSystemMismatchError` regardless.
- **SQL is 0-based.** `pb.register_*` + `pb.sql` return 0-based half-open
  starts (BED 0 stays 0, VCF POS 10 becomes 9) whatever the global option,
  and the result has no metadata. Do not mix SQL output with `read_*` output
  or pass it to interval operations without converting and tagging it
  (`references/sql_processing.md`).
- Writing back to BED: subtract 1 from `start` of a 1-based frame first.

```python
import polars as pl
import polars_bio as pb

pb.set_option("datafusion.bio.coordinate_system_check", True)
peaks = pb.read_bed("peaks.bed", use_zero_based=True)        # BED numbers
genes = pl.DataFrame({"chrom": ["chr1"], "start": [999], "end": [2000]})
genes.config_meta.set(coordinate_system_zero_based=True)
hits = pb.overlap(peaks, genes, output_type="polars.DataFrame")
```

## Interval operations

All take `chrom`, `start`, `end` (override with `cols1`/`cols2` lists) and
return a LazyFrame unless `output_type="polars.DataFrame"`.

- `overlap(df1, df2)` — join of every overlapping pair, columns suffixed
  `_1`/`_2`; `overlap_output="left"` keeps df1 rows only.
- `count_overlaps(df1, df2)` — df1 plus `count` (0 when none).
- `nearest(df1, df2, k=1, overlap=True, distance=True)` — adds `distance`,
  0 for overlapping pairs.
- `coverage(df1, df2)` — df1 plus `coverage`, the bases of df1 covered by
  df2 (a `[1,10]` interval overlapped by `[5,7]` gets 3).
- `merge(df, min_dist=0)` — **overlapping intervals only.** Bookended
  intervals stay separate at `min_dist=0` and merge at `min_dist=1`;
  bioframe merges them at its default `min_dist=0`
  (https://bioframe.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api-intervalops.html). Adds
  `n_intervals`.
- `cluster`, `complement(df, view_df=genome)`, `subtract(df1, df2)`.
- The `.pb` accessor has interval operations on **LazyFrame** only;
  `DataFrame.pb` has only `write_*`.
- The first frame is the probe, the second is indexed: pass the smaller set
  second (`references/interval_operations.md`).

## Depth from BAM/CRAM: `pb.depth`

- **`coverage` is Int16 and wraps silently above 32,767**: 33,000 reads over
  one base came back as `-32536`. Assert `coverage.min() >= 0` on every
  result; for deep data (amplicons, mtDNA) use aii-kdense-pysam or samtools.
- Default `filter_flag=1796` drops unmapped, secondary, QC-fail and
  duplicate reads. There is no base-quality filter and orphan pairs count,
  so on the same toy column `pb.depth` gave 6 where pysam's default pileup
  gave 4. Name the tool and filters with any depth you report.
- Output is run-length blocks (`contig`, `pos_start`, `pos_end`,
  `coverage`) in the configured system; `per_base=True` emits every
  position from 1, zeros included.

## Readers

- Whole-file `read_bam`, `read_cram(..., reference_path=)` and `read_vcf`
  need no index (checked on unindexed BAM and CRAM).
- `scan_*` returns a LazyFrame for out-of-core work; select columns early.
- `read_vcf(info_fields=[...], samples=[...])` limits parsing to what you
  need.
- Cloud paths (`s3://`, `gs://`, `az://`) default to `allow_anonymous=True`;
  only public buckets are in scope (pods hold no cloud credentials).
- Readers return positions as UInt32 (BED, VCF) or Int32 (BAM, depth).
- Per-format columns: `references/file_io.md`.

## Parallelism

`datafusion.execution.target_partitions` defaults to 1 (single-threaded).
Set it from the CPU budget in aii-use-hardware, not `os.cpu_count()` on a
shared machine: `pb.set_option("datafusion.execution.target_partitions", 8)`.

## Reporting

State `polars_bio.__version__`, the coordinate system of every input and
output, `min_dist` for merges, and for depth the flag filter and the
overflow check.

## References

- `references/interval_operations.md` — every operation's parameters and
  output columns.
- `references/file_io.md` — readers, writers, schemas, cloud options.
- `references/sql_processing.md` — register functions and SQL, 0-based.
- `references/pileup_operations.md` — `depth` parameters and schemas.
- `references/configuration.md` — options, coordinate metadata, logging.
- `references/bioframe_migration.md` — mapping from bioframe and the three
  silent differences.
skills.description: Genomic interval algebra (overlap, nearest, merge, coverage, complement, subtract) and BED/VCF/BAM/GFF reading on Polars with polars-bio, including its 1-based default, SQL tables that stay 0-based and an Int16 depth overflow. Use when intersecting or merging interval sets at scale in Python or porting bioframe code. NOT for per-read BAM/VCF logic (use aii-kdense-pysam) or format conversion rules (use aii-kdense-genomic-coordinates).
skills.compatibility: Python 3.12, uv; polars-bio==0.36.0 (polars 1.44); network: none unless reading s3://, gs:// or az:// paths (anonymous by default); GPU: none.

skills.content:
# pysam: HTSlib files from Python

pysam wraps HTSlib, samtools and bcftools. Every statement below was checked
against the installed pysam 0.24.1 (HTSlib 1.24) on 2026-09-24, by
introspection and toy files, unless it cites a spec. Run the scripts from the
skill directory as `python3 scripts/<name>.py`.

## Setup

```bash
uv venv .venv --python 3.12 && . .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -r <skill-dir>/requirements.txt
```

## Decide before writing code

1. Identify the real format, compression (BGZF, not plain gzip), sort order
   and index. `scripts/inspect_hts.py` reports all of them without reading
   records.
2. Pick one coordinate form per call: numeric arguments or a region string.
3. For CRAM, name the exact reference FASTA of the assembly it was written
   against.
4. Prefer indexed region access; scan sequentially only on purpose.
5. Write to a new path with a copied header; never overwrite the input.
6. State the read filter in the output: flags, MAPQ, base quality, overlap
   and orphan handling, depth cap.

## The coordinate contract

- **Numeric arguments are 0-based, half-open** in `AlignmentFile.fetch`,
  `count`, `count_coverage`, `pileup`, `VariantFile.fetch`,
  `FastaFile.fetch` and `TabixFile.fetch`.
- **Region strings are 1-based, inclusive** (samtools syntax).
  `bam.fetch("chr1", 99, 199)` and `bam.fetch(region="chr1:100-199")` select
  the same 100 bases.
- `VariantRecord.pos` is the 1-based VCF `POS`; `.start` is 0-based and
  `.stop` is 0-based exclusive (`start + len(ref)` for simple alleles).
- `AlignedSegment.reference_start` is 0-based; `reference_end` points one past
  the last aligned base.
- Region fetch needs an index and returns records **overlapping** the region,
  not contained in it; `fetch(until_eof=True)` streams every record,
  unplaced unmapped reads included, without an index.

Full conversion table, overlap vs containment and index limits:
`references/coordinates_and_indexing.md`.

## Depth and count traps (verified, pysam 0.24.1)

The same region gives four different "depths" depending on the call. Say
which one you report.

- `count()` — defaults to `read_callback="nofilter"`: duplicates, secondary,
  QC-fail and unmapped-placed records all count. `read_callback="all"` drops
  those four flags. An unknown callback string raises a confusing
  `'str' object is not callable`.
- `count_coverage()` — `quality_threshold=15` (inclusive) and
  `read_callback="all"`; orphan pairs are kept; only A/C/G/T are counted.
- `pileup()` — defaults `stepper="samtools"`, `min_base_quality=13`,
  `max_depth=8000`, `ignore_overlaps=True`, `ignore_orphans=True`,
  `flag_filter` = unmapped | secondary | QC-fail | duplicate,
  and BAQ recomputation (samtools stepper) when a `fastafile` is given
  (`pysam/libcalignmentfile.pyx:2462-2474`, v0.24.1). With
  `ignore_orphans=True`, paired reads not flagged proper-pair vanish: check
  the flag distribution first (`scripts/alignment_qc.py`).
- `PileupColumn.n` / `nsegments` count reads **before** the base-quality
  filter; `get_num_aligned()`, `pileups` and `get_query_sequences()` apply
  it. Toy column: `n` 5, `get_num_aligned()` 4.
- `pileup()` takes its options as `**kwargs` read with `kwargs.get`, so a
  misspelled option (`min_mapq=30`, `min_base_qual=0`) is silently ignored
  and the default applies. Spell them exactly: `min_mapping_quality`,
  `min_base_quality`, `max_depth`, `ignore_orphans`, `ignore_overlaps`,
  `flag_filter`, `flag_require`, `compute_baq`, `truncate`.
- Without `truncate=True`, pileup yields columns outside the requested
  interval wherever reads overhang it.
- `max_depth` caps reads per column; at >8000x (amplicon, mtDNA) raise it or
  the depth silently plateaus.
- `AlignedSegment.query_length` is 0 when SEQ is `*` (common for secondary
  alignments); use `infer_read_length()` (from CIGAR, hard clips included)
  for read length.
- MAPQ 255 means "unavailable" in the SAM spec (SAMv1 §1.4) but passes any
  numeric `mapping_quality >= t` test; STAR also writes 255 for unique
  mappers (STAR manual, `--outSAMmapqUnique`). Decide per aligner, and say
  so.

```python
for col in bam.pileup("chr1", 999, 2_000, truncate=True, stepper="samtools",
                      fastafile=fasta, min_mapping_quality=20,
                      min_base_quality=20, max_depth=100_000):
    depth = col.get_num_aligned()
```

## Variants

- `VariantFile` detects VCF/BCF and compression itself; `.format`
  (`"VCF"`/`"BCF"`) and `.compression` (`"BGZF"`, `"GZIP"`, `"NONE"`) say
  what it found. A plain-gzip `.vcf.gz` does not open at all
  (`NotImplementedError: seek not implemented in files compressed by method
  1`); recompress with bgzip. `scripts/inspect_hts.py` names the problem.
- Call `subset_samples([...])` before reading any record; it avoids decoding
  the other samples' FORMAT fields.
- `record.samples[s]["GT"]` is a tuple with `None` for a missing allele;
  `call.get("GT")` is `None` when the record has no GT field at all.
  `call.phased` gives the separator.
- `record.filter.keys()` is `["PASS"]` for PASS and empty for `.`: "no filter
  applied" is not "passed".
- To add INFO/FORMAT/FILTER fields, declare them in a copied header first,
  then `record.translate(out.header)` before assigning; never rebuild
  `header.samples` by hand. Details: `references/variant_files.md`.

## CRAM, threads, wrapped tools

- New CRAM output is version 3.1 (checked: file magic `CRAM\x03\x01`), and
  HTSlib >= 1.22 no longer fetches references from the EBI server by default
  (pysam NEWS, 0.24.0 and 0.24.1). Pass `reference_filename=` explicitly;
  set `REF_PATH`/`REF_CACHE` only for deliberate MD5 lookup, with the cache
  under the workspace.
- `threads=` speeds up BGZF/CRAM (de)compression only, not Python loops.
  One handle per iterator: use `multiple_iterators=True` or reopen per
  thread/process (`references/cram_and_performance.md`).
- `import pysam.samtools` / `pysam.bcftools`; pass each CLI token as a
  separate string. Dispatchers capture stdout by default: for large output
  use `-o path` with `catch_stdout=False`. Failures raise
  `pysam.SamtoolsError`.
- `pysam.tabix_compress` then `pysam.tabix_index(..., preset="bed"|"gff"|"vcf")`
  on coordinate-sorted input; use CSI (`csi=True`) when a contig exceeds
  2^29 bp, the BAI/TBI limit (SAMv1 §5.2). `tabix_index` on an uncompressed
  file compresses it and **deletes the original** unless
  `keep_original=True`.

## Writing

- Open output with `template=` (or a copied header) and preserve sort order
  if it will be indexed.
- Set `query_sequence` before `query_qualities` (setting the sequence
  resets the qualities).
- Prefer `pysam.CIGAR_OPS` members; `pysam.CMATCH` and friends are
  compatibility aliases.
- Validate: `pysam.samtools.quickcheck("-v", path)` for alignments; reopen
  VCF/FASTA outputs and read one record.

## Scripts

All four read local files only, refuse to overwrite outputs, exit 2 on bad
input, and print JSON. `--help` documents coordinates and privacy flags.

- `scripts/inspect_hts.py FILE [--reference ref.fa]` — format, BGZF vs
  plain gzip (refused for VCF, FASTA and tabix), index, sort order, contigs,
  header keys; no record scan.
- `scripts/alignment_qc.py IN.bam [--region chr1:1-1000000]
  [--max-records N]` — flag counts, mapping/duplicate/proper-pair rates,
  mean read length (records with a stored SEQ only), mean MAPQ (255
  excluded).
- `scripts/variant_summary.py IN.vcf.gz [--region R] [--sample S]` —
  SNV/MNV/indel/symbolic counts, FILTER labels, Ts/Tv on biallelic SNVs,
  genotype and ploidy counts.
- `scripts/filter_alignments.py IN.bam OUT.bam [--min-mapq Q]
  [--exclude-duplicates ...] [--index]` — order-preserving filter with
  per-reason exclusion counts.

## Reporting

State pysam and HTSlib versions (`pysam.__version__`,
`pysam.__samtools_version__`), the region form, the read filter and which
depth definition you used.

## References

- `references/alignment_files.md` — flags, CIGAR, tags, modified bases,
  pileup, writing.
- `references/variant_files.md` — headers, records, samples, writing,
  translation, indexing.
- `references/sequence_files.md` — FASTA/FASTQ records, BGZF and tabix.
- `references/coordinates_and_indexing.md` — conversions, overlap, BAI vs
  CSI, contig names.
- `references/cram_and_performance.md` — CRAM references, remote I/O,
  threads.
- `references/common_workflows.md` — integrated analysis patterns.
- `references/api_reference.md` — signatures and defaults.
- `references/migration_to_0_24.md` — upgrade notes.
- `references/sources.md` — docs, specs and release sources.
skills.description: Read, query, filter and write SAM/BAM/CRAM, VCF/BCF, FASTA/FASTQ and tabix files with pysam (HTSlib): the 0-based vs region-string coordinate contract, pileup and coverage defaults that change depth, CRAM references, and streaming QC CLIs. Use when a task opens NGS files in Python or counts reads, depth or genotypes. NOT for coordinate conversion across formats (use aii-kdense-genomic-coordinates) or signal tracks (use aii-kdense-deeptools).
skills.compatibility: Python 3.12, uv; pysam==0.24.1 (HTSlib/samtools/bcftools 1.24, manylinux wheels for x86-64 and ARM); network: none; GPU: none. CRAM needs the matching reference FASTA.

# scikit-bio: community diversity and biological data in Python

Decide by the rules below and log each choice with its reason; never wait
for confirmation. Every behaviour named here was run against
scikit-bio 0.7.4 on 2026-09-24; the traps are pinned in the unit tests.

## Setup

Run from the skill directory.

```bash
uv venv .venv --python 3.12 && . .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Router

- count table plus sample groups to diversity, PCoA and tests — run:
  `python3 scripts/community_diversity.py --table counts.tsv
  --orientation samples-by-features --metadata meta.tsv --group-column site
  --out-dir div`; read: `references/diversity_and_stats.md`
- single metrics, ordination options, Mantel, BIOENV, ANCOM,
  `dirmult_ttest` — read: `references/diversity_and_stats.md`
- sequences, translation, pairwise alignment, `TreeNode`, file formats,
  protein embeddings — read: `references/sequences_trees_io.md`
- a tree from sequences — use aii-kdense-phylogenetics, then load its rooted
  Newick here for Faith PD or UniFrac

## Decision rules

1. **Raw integer counts in, samples as rows.** Refuse relative abundances:
   richness estimators (`chao1`, `observed_features`) and depth-based
   methods silently give wrong numbers on proportions. State the
   orientation; BIOM exports are features-by-samples.
2. **Rarefy once, for diversity only.** With uneven depth, subsample every
   sample to one depth (the shallowest sample at or above 1000 reads is
   this skill's default), drop and list the shallower ones, fix the seed
   (Schloss 2024, doi:10.1128/msphere.00354-23). For differential abundance
   do not rarefy; use a compositional model such as `dirmult_ttest`
   (McMurdie & Holmes 2014, doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003531).
3. **Join metadata by sample ID, never by row order**, and refuse missing
   or extra IDs. Pass groupings as a DataFrame plus `column`.
4. **Pick metrics by question:** observed features and Shannon (natural
   log; state the base) for within-sample diversity; Bray-Curtis for
   abundance, Jaccard for membership, UniFrac when phylogeny matters
   (Lozupone & Knight 2005, doi:10.1128/AEM.71.12.8228-8235.2005).
5. **Phylogenetic metrics need a rooted tree that covers every feature.**
   Root on an outgroup when there is one, else at the midpoint, and report
   which; the values change with the root.
6. **PERMANOVA always with PERMDISP.** PERMANOVA's pseudo-F responds to
   differences in spread as well as location (Anderson 2001,
   doi:10.1111/j.1442-9993.2001.01070.pp.x). If PERMDISP (Anderson 2006,
   doi:10.1111/j.1541-0420.2005.00440.x) is significant at 0.05, report
   that the groups differ in dispersion and do not claim a shift in
   centroid from PERMANOVA alone. Use 999 permutations or more, and state
   the smallest attainable p for small designs.
7. **Report PCoA shares from the full decomposition** and mention the
   negative-eigenvalue warning for non-Euclidean metrics.
8. **One test per question.** For several metrics, report all of them;
   do not pick the one that gives the smallest p.

## Traps (verified 2026-09-24)

- `alpha.shannon(x)` — what happens: natural log since 0.6.1 (base 2
  before), so values differ from older pipelines by ln 2; do instead:
  state the base, or `base=2` to match bits
- `alpha_diversity("chao1", proportions)` — what happens: no error; with no
  singletons the estimate collapses to the observed count; do instead:
  raw counts (the script refuses non-integers)
- `simpson` — what happens: it is Gini-Simpson 1 - D; `dominance` is D;
  do instead: name the index you report
- `permanova(dm, groups_list)` — what happens: a list is matched to
  `dm.ids` by position, so a list in metadata order mislabels samples
  without error; do instead: `permanova(dm, meta_df, column="site")`
- `permdisp(dm, ...)` defaults — what happens: dispersion is measured in 10
  PCoA axes (F 15.05 vs 15.71 with all axes on a 40-sample test), and fewer
  than 10 samples raise `cannot extend distance matrix size`; do instead:
  `dimensions=len(dm.ids)`
- `pcoa(dm, dimensions=3).proportion_explained` — what happens: divided by
  the trace, not the positive eigenvalues, so PC1 read 31.1 % instead of
  30.1 %; do instead: run full PCoA, then keep the axes you plot
- seeded `permanova` — what happens: OpenMP threads made the same seed give
  p = 0.001 or 0.002 across runs; do instead: `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` before
  importing scikit-bio (the script sets it)
- `mantel(a.data, b.data)` — what happens: arrays are matched by position;
  do instead: pass two `DistanceMatrix` objects (matched by ID)
- `faith_pd` / UniFrac on an unrooted tree — what happens: `ValueError: The
  tree must be rooted`; a feature not in the tree raises `MissingNodeError`
- support read as node names, then `root_at_midpoint()` — what happens:
  the label stays on its node and now describes another split; do
  instead: `tree.assign_supports()` first
- `tree.compare_rfd(other)` — what happens: a bifurcating root is taken as
  rooted, two rootings of one tree score 2; do instead: `rooted=False`
  (`rf_dists` already defaults to unrooted)
- `pair_align(a, b)` "global" — what happens: `free_ends=True` by default,
  end gaps are free; do instead: `free_ends=False` for Needleman-Wunsch
- `ancom(table, ...)` or `clr(table)` with zeros — what happens: `Input
  matrix must have strictly positive components`; do instead:
  `multi_replace` or a stated pseudocount, or `dirmult_ttest`
- `ProteinEmbedding(...).to_distances()` (upstream) — what happens:
  `AttributeError`; do instead: `embed_vec_to_distances(vectors)`

## Script

`scripts/community_diversity.py` refuses (exit 2) before any analysis
when counts are negative or not integers, table and metadata sample IDs
differ, a group has fewer than two samples, tree tips do not cover every
feature, a metric name is unknown, or permutations are below 99. It
rarefies (`--rarefy-depth auto|none|N`, `--min-depth 1000`, `--seed 1`),
midpoint-roots an unrooted `--tree` and logs it, computes `--alpha`
(default `observed_features,shannon,simpson`) with Kruskal-Wallis tests,
and for each `--beta` metric (default `braycurtis,jaccard`) a distance
matrix, full PCoA, PERMANOVA and PERMDISP with all axes.

```bash
python3 scripts/community_diversity.py --table counts.tsv \
    --orientation samples-by-features --metadata meta.tsv \
    --group-column site --out-dir div --tree features.nwk \
    --alpha observed_features,shannon,faith_pd \
    --beta braycurtis,unweighted_unifrac,weighted_unifrac
```

Outputs: `alpha.tsv`, `alpha_tests.tsv`, `beta_<metric>.tsv`,
`pcoa_<metric>.tsv` (axis labels carry the explained share),
`beta_tests.tsv` (`permanova_pseudo_F`, `permanova_p`, `permdisp_F`,
`permdisp_p`), and `run.json` (scikit-bio version, depth, dropped samples, tree
rooting, Shannon base, thread count, and `dispersion_differs`: the
metrics whose PERMDISP p < 0.05).

## Reporting

State the table orientation and source, the rarefaction depth and dropped
samples (or why no rarefaction), each metric with its variant (log base,
weighted or not, normalised or not), tree source and rooting,
permutations and seed, PERMANOVA and PERMDISP results side by side, and
the PCoA share per axis. Figures go through aii-data-fig-gen.

## References

- `references/diversity_and_stats.md`: input checks, alpha and beta
  metrics, PCoA, PERMANOVA/PERMDISP/ANOSIM/Mantel, compositional
  differential abundance, with signatures and sources.
- `references/sequences_trees_io.md`: sequence classes, translation,
  `pair_align`, `TreeNode` rooting and comparison, tree builders, file
  formats, embeddings.
skills.description: Microbiome and community ecology with scikit-bio 0.7: rarefied alpha and beta diversity (Shannon, Faith PD, Bray-Curtis, UniFrac), PCoA, PERMANOVA with PERMDISP, Mantel, compositional differential abundance, plus sequence, alignment, tree and format I/O. Use when analysing a count table against sample groups, or reading FASTA/FASTQ/Newick/BIOM in Python. NOT for inferring trees from sequences (use aii-kdense-phylogenetics).
skills.compatibility: Python 3.12, uv; scikit-bio 0.7.4, numpy, pandas, scipy pinned in requirements.txt; network: none; GPU: none.

skills.content:
# Statistics for autonomous research

Decide by the rules below, log each decision and its reason in the output,
and never wait for confirmation. Library facts were checked on 2026-09-24
against the versions in `requirements.txt`.

## Setup

```bash
uv venv .venv --python 3.12 && . .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -r <skill-dir>/requirements.txt
```

Scripts are importable modules or CLIs in `scripts/`; run CLIs with
`python scripts/<name>.py --help`. Plots are headless; `assumption_checks`
saves its figures when `KDENSE_STATS_FIG_DIR` is set.

## Router

- compare ML methods over seeds and benchmarks — read:
  `references/ml_evaluation.md`; run: `scripts/compare_runs.py`
- design: unit, randomisation, blocking, factorial or ablation, sequential
  looks — read: `references/design.md`; run: `scripts/randomization.py`,
  `scripts/doe_designs.py`
- how many subjects, samples or seeds — read: `references/power.md`; run:
  `scripts/power.py`, `scripts/simulate_power.py`
- which test; assumptions; outliers; missing data — read:
  `references/tests_and_assumptions.md`; run: `scripts/assumption_checks.py`
- effect sizes, conversions, CIs — read: `references/effect_sizes.md`
- regression, GLM, counts, robust or cluster SEs — read:
  `references/regression_glm.md`
- two measurement methods agree? detection limits — read:
  `references/method_comparison.md`
- Bayesian alternative, ArviZ 1.x API — read: `references/bayesian.md`
- write-up templates, null results — read: `references/writing_results.md`

## Workflow and decision rules

1. **Fix the plan before the data.** Hypothesis, primary outcome, unit of
   analysis, test, alpha, SESOI, multiplicity family and correction, and
   exclusion rules, written into the run's output before any result exists.
   Anything chosen later is labelled exploratory.
2. **Identify the experimental unit.** The replicate is what the treatment is
   independently applied to: the animal not the cell, the training run (seed)
   not the test example, the cluster not the member (Hurlbert 1984,
   doi:10.2307/1942661). Analyse at that level or with a mixed model.
3. **Size the study** with `power.py` or, for anything non-standard,
   `simulate_power.py`, powered on the SESOI; add attrition, clustering and
   multiplicity; report a sensitivity range.
4. **Randomise and block** every nuisance factor you can name (batch, day,
   plate, GPU type, library version); record the seed and schedule.
5. **Analyse as planned**, with the effect size and its CI next to every p.
6. **Report everything planned**, including nulls, with the correction and
   the software versions.

Defaults when nothing else is specified:
- alpha = .05 two-sided; power .80 (.90 for a confirmatory headline claim).
- Two independent means: **Welch** t, never Student by default
  (Delacre et al. 2017, doi:10.5334/irsp.82).
- Heavy tails, ordinal data or small n with outliers: rank or permutation
  test, chosen before looking.
- Multiplicity: **Holm** over the pre-declared family; Benjamini-Hochberg for
  large exploratory screens. Tukey HSD or Games-Howell for all pairwise
  post-hoc comparisons.
- Confidence level 95%; bootstrap with >= 9,999 resamples and a fixed seed.
- Requests for post-hoc "observed power": give the MDE at the achieved n and
  the effect CI instead, and say why (Hoenig & Heisey 2001,
  doi:10.1198/000313001300339897).

## ML comparisons (the most common case here)

- **Seeds are the replicates.** Use at least 5 seeds per method x task for any
  comparative claim, 10 when the expected gap is within about 2 seed-SDs; the
  same seed set for every method; seeds that vary init, data order and split
  (Bouthillier et al. 2021, arXiv:2103.03098). The 5/10 floor is this skill's
  rule; plan the real number by simulation from a pilot seed SD.
- **Pair what is paired.** Same seed across methods -> paired t on per-seed
  differences; one fixed test set and two trained models -> McNemar or a
  paired bootstrap over examples (Dietterich 1998,
  doi:10.1162/089976698300017197). Never a plain t-test over CV folds
  (Nadeau & Bengio 2003, doi:10.1023/A:1024068626366).
- **Across benchmarks:** per-task means, then Wilcoxon signed-rank vs the
  baseline with Holm across methods, plus win/tie/loss and a two-stage
  bootstrap CI (tasks, then seeds) of the mean difference (Demšar 2006, JMLR
  7:1-30; Benavoli et al. 2016, JMLR 17(5)). Fewer than 6 tasks cannot reach
  p < .05 with Wilcoxon: report the CI, not a test.
- **Every method x task x metric cell is a hypothesis.** Correct across all of
  them (Holm, or BH for large screens), and make the headline the aggregate
  test, not a count of significant cells.
- **Bootstrap CIs:** t-based per cell when seeds are few (a percentile
  bootstrap over 3-10 values is too narrow; Hesterberg 2015,
  doi:10.1080/00031305.2015.1089789); bootstrap across tasks or examples.
- **Tune every method with the same budget on validation data**; select
  checkpoints and seeds on validation only; report all runs, crashed ones
  included, with the handling rule fixed in advance.

```bash
python scripts/compare_runs.py runs.csv --baseline erm            # columns: method, task, seed, score
python scripts/compare_runs.py runs.csv --baseline erm --metric error --lower-is-better \
    --correction fdr_bh --relative --json comparison.json
```

## Verified library traps

- `pg.ttest(x, y)` — trap: default `correction="auto"` uses Welch only when
  `len(x) != len(y)`, not when variances differ (pingouin 0.6.1,
  `parametric.py:255`); fix: `pg.ttest(x, y, correction=True)`
- `pg.ttest(..., alternative="greater")` — trap: drops the `BF10` column;
  `pg.bayesfactor_ttest` raises for one-sided; fix: posterior probability from
  a model (`references/bayesian.md`)
- pingouin >= 0.6 columns — trap: renamed: `p_val`, `p_unc`, `cohen_d`,
  `CI95`, `U_val`, `W_val` (0.5.x: `p-val`, `cohen-d`, `CI95%`, `p-unc`); fix:
  use the new names
- `multipletests(p)` — trap: default `method="hs"` (Holm-Sidak), not Holm
  (statsmodels 0.15.0); fix: always pass `method="holm"` or `"fdr_bh"`
- `FTestAnovaPower().solve_power(...)` — trap: argument is `k_groups`; result
  is **total** n; fix: divide by k, round up
- `sm.OLS(y, X)` — trap: no intercept unless X has one; fix:
  `sm.add_constant(X)` or the formula API
- `sm.families.NegativeBinomial()` in a GLM — trap: dispersion fixed at alpha
  = 1.0, not estimated; fix: `smf.negativebinomial(...)` estimates alpha
- `az.summary(trace)` — trap: ArviZ 1.x reports 89% equal-tailed intervals by
  default; fix: `ci_prob=0.95`
- `scipy.stats.levene` — trap: default `center="median"` is Brown-Forsythe;
  fix: say so, or pass `center="mean"`
- `scipy.stats.bootstrap(..., random_state=)` — trap: legacy `RandomState`
  path (SPEC 7, scipy >= 1.15), no warning; fix:
  `rng=np.random.default_rng(seed)`
- `simulate_power(..., alpha=)` — trap: ignored when `gen_and_test` returns a
  bool; fix: return the p-value (a float)

## Effect sizes and power in one screen

- Report an effect size with a CI for every test; prefer raw units. Cohen's
  small/medium/large (d 0.2/0.5/0.8, f 0.10/0.25/0.40, r 0.1/0.3/0.5) are for
  planning when nothing better exists, never for interpretation.
- Reference values (statsmodels 0.15.0, alpha .05 two-sided, power .80):
  d = 0.5 needs 64 per group; d = 0.4, 100; d = 0.6, 45; ANOVA f = 0.25 with
  k = 3 needs 158 in total.
- Inflate for attrition n / (1 - rate) and clustering DEFF = 1 + (m - 1) ICC.
- A null result is "no significant difference" plus the effect CI and the
  MDE; equivalence needs TOST against a pre-stated margin.

## Folded rules

- **Regression and counts** (from statsmodels): check Poisson overdispersion
  (Pearson chi^2 / df well above 1 -> negative binomial); use HC3 SEs for
  heteroskedasticity and cluster-robust SEs (>= ~30-50 clusters) or a mixed
  model for clustering; logit and log-link coefficients are on the link scale,
  so exponentiate for odds or rate ratios and give marginal effects for
  probabilities. Details: `references/regression_glm.md`.
- **Method comparison** (from analytical-method-validation): agreement is
  never a correlation; use Bland-Altman bias and limits of agreement (Bland &
  Altman 1986, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(86)90837-8) and Deming or
  Passing-Bablok regression, never OLS. Detection limits DL = 3.3 sigma / S,
  QL = 10 sigma / S with the sigma source named (ICH Q2(R2) section 3.2.3.3).
  Details: `references/method_comparison.md`.

## Integrity rules

- One planned analysis per hypothesis. No test shopping, outlier-rule
  shopping, subgroup fishing or re-running seeds until a difference is
  significant; if you ran it, report it.
- Significance is not importance; lead with the effect size.
- "Significant in A but not in B" is not a test of A vs B; test the
  difference (Gelman & Stern 2006, doi:10.1198/000313006X152649).
- Label outputs as unreviewed research output; never claim clinical or
  regulatory validity.

## Scripts

- `scripts/compare_runs.py`: CLI; seeds x tasks comparison vs a baseline
  (per-cell t CIs, paired or Welch tests with Holm/BH, Wilcoxon + sign test +
  two-stage bootstrap across tasks, Friedman omnibus).
- `scripts/power.py`: `sample_size`, `power`, `mde`, `power_curve` over
  statsmodels for t, ANOVA, proportions, correlation, chi-square, regression.
- `scripts/simulate_power.py`: `simulate_power`, `find_sample_size`, with
  worked two-group, logistic, cluster-randomised and mixed-model examples.
- `scripts/randomization.py`: seeded simple, block, stratified-block and
  cluster allocation schedules; `arm_balance`.
- `scripts/doe_designs.py`: full and fractional factorial, Plackett-Burman,
  central composite, Box-Behnken, Latin hypercube, in real units with
  randomised run order.
- `scripts/assumption_checks.py`: normality, variance, linearity, outliers
  and OLS diagnostics as dicts with interpretations.
skills.description: Plan, run and report statistical analyses: design, randomisation, power and sample size, test choice, effect sizes with CIs, multiplicity, and ML comparisons across seeds and benchmarks (paired tests, bootstrap CIs, Holm/FDR over cells). Scripts: power, simulation, DOE, run comparison. Use when designing an experiment, choosing n or seeds, testing a hypothesis, comparing methods, or writing up results. NOT for PyMC modelling (PyMC directly) or ML pipelines and metrics (use aii-kdense-ml-eval).
skills.compatibility: Python 3.12, uv; numpy, scipy, pandas, statsmodels, pingouin, matplotlib, pyDOE3 pinned in requirements.txt; network: none; GPU: none.

skills.name: aii-kdense-tiledbvcf
skills.content:
# TileDB-VCF: many single-sample VCFs as one dataset

TileDB-VCF stores single-sample VCF/BCF files in a sparse TileDB array so a
region can be read across thousands of samples, and new samples are appended
without re-merging a cohort VCF. Every API statement below was read from the
0.40.3 source (links at the end) on 2026-09-24; the library could not be run
here (no linux-aarch64 build), so the pre-flight script is the tested part.

## Install

Not on PyPI. From the `tiledb` conda channel, pinned:

```bash
micromamba create -y -n tiledbvcf -c conda-forge -c bioconda -c tiledb \
    python=3.12 tiledbvcf-py=0.40.3
```

Builds exist for linux-64, osx-64 and osx-arm64 only (anaconda.org
`tiledb/tiledbvcf-py`, checked 2026-09-24). On linux-aarch64 use an x86-64
machine or the `tiledb/tiledbvcf-py` Docker image under emulation, and say
so. Do not install `tiledb-cloud` or use a TileDB Cloud account: that is the
paid service and is out of scope.

## Before ingesting: run the pre-flight

```bash
python3 scripts/preflight_ingest.py --list vcfs.txt --write-samples-file samples.tsv
tiledbvcf store --uri cohort_ds -f samples.tsv    # or ingest_samples(), below
```

It refuses what TileDB-VCF 0.40.3 rejects mid-run or ingests wrongly:

- **Combined (multi-sample) VCFs are refused**: "a file has more than 1
  sample. Ingestion from cVCF is not supported" (`writer.cc:710-716`). Split
  with `bcftools +split` or `bcftools view -s` first.
- **An index is required**, looked up as `<file>.csi` then `<file>.tbi`, or
  given per line as `<vcf>\t<index>` in the samples file
  (`sample_utils.cc:68-100`). A plain-gzip VCF cannot be indexed: `bgzip` it.
- **Sample names must be unique**; the name comes from the header, and a
  sites-only file is stored under the empty name (`writer.cc:707-716`).
- **One contig style** ("chr1" or "1") across all files: a region string
  names one style, so samples stored under the other silently return no rows.

Exit 0 all pass, 1 a check failed, 2 bad arguments; `--json` for machines.

## API (0.40.3) and its traps

```python
import tiledbvcf

ds = tiledbvcf.Dataset("cohort_ds", mode="w")
ds.create_dataset(extra_attrs=["fmt_DP", "info_AF"])   # a LIST, not "fmt_DP,info_AF"
ds.ingest_samples(sample_uris=paths, threads=8, total_memory_budget_mb=8192)

ds = tiledbvcf.Dataset("cohort_ds", mode="r",
                       cfg=tiledbvcf.ReadConfig(memory_budget_mb=4096))
frames = list(ds.read_iter(attrs=["sample_name", "contig", "pos_start", "pos_end",
                                  "alleles", "fmt_GT"],
                           regions=["chr1:1000000-2000000"], samples=["S1", "S2"]))
```

- **`read()` can return part of the answer.** When results exceed the memory
  budget it returns what fit; `read_completed()` is then False and the rest
  comes from `continue_read()` (`dataset.py:548-552`). Use `read_iter()`, or
  loop until `read_completed()`. Never report counts from one `read()`.
- **An empty frame can be an error.** `continue_read_arrow` wraps result
  retrieval in a bare `except:` that returns an empty table
  (`dataset.py:785-789`). For "no variants here", confirm with
  `ds.count(regions=..., samples=...)`, which raises on a bad read status.
- **Regions are strings `contig:start-end`, 1-based and closed.** Start 0
  raises "Regions must be 1-based"; a bare `"chr1"` or `chr1:1,000-2,000`
  raises; a contig name containing `:` (HLA alleles in GRCh38 analysis sets)
  cannot be expressed (`dataset.py:117-134`). BED numbers pasted into a
  region string are off by one at the start without any error; pass BED
  files as `bed_file=` instead.
- **Overlapping and adjacent regions are merged and sorted** before the
  query (`dataset.py:264-277`), so rows cannot be attributed back to an input
  region; intersect afterwards if you need per-region labels.
- **`ReadConfig` fields**: `limit, region_partition, sample_partition,
  sort_regions, memory_budget_mb, tiledb_config, buffer_percentage,
  tiledb_tile_cache_percentage` (`dataset.py:22-67`). The field is
  `memory_budget_mb` (default 2048); `memory_budget=` raises TypeError.
  `limit` truncates reads by design. `region_partition=(i, n)` and
  `sample_partition=(i, n)` split one query across n workers; they are not
  schema settings.
- **In `mode="w"` only `cfg.tiledb_config` is applied** (`dataset.py:235-262`);
  ingestion memory goes to `ingest_samples(total_memory_budget_mb=...)` or
  `total_memory_percentage=`. `cfg` and `tiledb_config=` are mutually
  exclusive in the constructor.
- **`create_dataset(extra_attrs=...)` joins with `","`** (`dataset.py:904`):
  the string `"fmt_DP"` becomes `f,m,t,_,D,P`. Pass a list. Extra
  attributes are fixed at creation; `vcf_attrs=<vcf>` materialises every
  INFO/FORMAT field of that file instead. `create_dataset` raises if the
  dataset exists (`dataset.py:941`). Defaults: `allow_duplicates=True`,
  allele-count, variant-stats and sample-stats arrays on.
- **Ingestion** appends; re-open with `mode="w"` to add samples. `resume=True`
  retries a partially ingested batch; `sample_batch_size` defaults to 10.
  `delete_samples(names)` also updates the stats arrays unless
  `skip_aggregate_stats=True`, which leaves them stale.
- **`Dataset.delete(uri)` runs `shutil.rmtree(uri)` on any existing local
  path** without checking it is a dataset (`dataset.py:1269-1270`). Check the
  path first.
- **Export**: `export(samples, regions, output_format="z", output_dir=".")`
  writes one file per sample into the current directory by default; set
  `output_dir`. `merge=True` needs `output_path` (`dataset.py:614-696`).
  Formats: `b` BCF, `u` uncompressed BCF, `z` vcf.gz, `v` VCF, `t` TSV (CLI).
- **Stats**: `ds.read_variant_stats(regions=[...])` and
  `ds.read_allele_count(regions=[...])` read the arrays built at ingestion;
  a dataset created with `enable_variant_stats=False` has none.
  `tiledbvcf.read_allele_frequency(uri, region)` is a thin
  wrapper that passes the deprecated `region=` argument.
  `tiledbvcf.sample_qc(uri, samples=[...])` returns per-sample QC metrics.

## CLI (same library)

`tiledbvcf create | store | export | list | stat | delete | utils`, each
with `--uri`. `export -r chr1:1-1000,chr2:5-50` or `-R regions.bed`,
`-s S1,S2` or `-f names.txt`, `-O z|v|b|u|t`, `-t CHR,POS,REF,ALT,F:GT`
for TSV fields, `-c` count only, `-n N` record limit. `store -f` reads
`<vcf>\t<index>` lines (`cli/tiledbvcf.cc:535-590, 736-830`).

## Report

State the tiledbvcf-py version and platform, the dataset URI, sample count
(`ds.sample_count()`), the exact region strings (1-based) and samples queried,
whether every read completed (`read_completed()`), and the pre-flight result.

## Sources

- TileDB-VCF 0.40.3 source, Python API:
  https://github.com/TileDB-Inc/TileDB-VCF/blob/0.40.3/apis/python/src/tiledbvcf/dataset.py
- Sample and index handling:
  https://github.com/TileDB-Inc/TileDB-VCF/blob/0.40.3/libtiledbvcf/src/utils/sample_utils.cc
- Single-sample check:
  https://github.com/TileDB-Inc/TileDB-VCF/blob/0.40.3/libtiledbvcf/src/write/writer.cc
- CLI: https://github.com/TileDB-Inc/TileDB-VCF/blob/0.40.3/libtiledbvcf/src/cli/tiledbvcf.cc
- Conda builds: https://anaconda.org/tiledb/tiledbvcf-py/files
- Docs: https://tiledb-inc.github.io/TileDB-VCF/
skills.description: Store and query many single-sample VCF/BCF files as one TileDB-VCF dataset (tiledbvcf-py 0.40.3, open source, local or S3/GCS/Azure paths): pre-flight the inputs, create, ingest, read by region and sample, export, and read variant stats. Use when a cohort of per-sample gVCFs/VCFs must be queried by region across samples or grown one sample at a time. NOT for reading one VCF (use aii-kdense-pysam) or for paid TileDB Cloud.
skills.compatibility: tiledbvcf-py==0.40.3 is conda-only (tiledb channel; linux-64, osx-64, osx-arm64; no linux-aarch64, not on PyPI). The pre-flight script needs Python 3.12 + pysam==0.24.1 (requirements.txt). network: none for local datasets; GPU: none.
